A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from SweetTokenizer to SweetTok. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, generation, few-shot classification, and ablation results in Tables 1–6, with additional ImageNet generation results in appendix Table 8.

after.justification: V3 reports original reconstruction, video generation, classification, and ablation results, including generator scaling and additional reconstruction metrics in appendix Table 8.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming CQAE to DQAE, the default codebook embeddings switch from Qwen to CLIP. V1's image-pretraining, video-proxy-training, and pixel-finetuning sequence becomes video training with proxy codes for the first 500K steps and without them for the next 500K, plus separate image finetuning (v3 Section 6.4 and Table 9). The decoupled architecture and part-of-speech codebook split remain.

E1.justification: V3 removes the entire class-conditional ImageNet image-generation evaluation documented in v1 Section 7.1, Table 8, and Figure 9. It retains video reconstruction on UCF-101/K-600, UCF-101 video generation, ImageNet reconstruction, and miniImageNet/UCF-101 few-shot classification. Thus task coverage contracts despite retaining the datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds LARP variants to video reconstruction and generation comparisons, MAGVIT-V2 to reconstruction, and MAGVIT/MAGVIT-V2 AR and MLM entries to generation (Tables 1–2). TokenFlow joins ImageNet reconstruction in Table 3. The removed image-generation evaluation also removes its comparator set. OmniTok is the renamed OmniTokenizer baseline.

E3.justification: Reported training settings change substantially: Table 9 replaces three training stages with 500K-step image finetuning and 1000K-step video training. V3 adds a 1.9B-parameter generator experiment and PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS evaluation. It also includes and explicitly separates 128×128 baseline results from 256×256 results. These are reported protocol changes; exact batch settings remain inconsistent between the main text and appendix.

E4.justification: V1's training-stage ablations are replaced by compression comparisons involving linear downsampling, LARP-style queries, and DQAE (Table 4). V3 removes the ImageNet codebook ablation while retaining revised video codebook comparisons (Table 5), and adds generator-size scaling analysis. These change the experimental questions examined, beyond updating scores.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional metrics in v3 do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported UCF-101 reconstruction rFVD changes from 44.35 to 20.46 for the compressed model and from 18.74 to 10.74 without compression. The 650M-generator gFVD changes from 128 to 84, with 65 newly reported for 1.9B parameters. These accompany method/training revisions, not controlled same-setting gains. Table 3 changes TiTok from 1.03 to 1.71; appendix Table 8 replaces image-generation results with reconstruction metrics. SweetTok's image rFID and few-shot accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's explicit three-stage loss definitions (Equations 6–8) are removed. V3 adds an explicit first-frame residual definition in Section 3.2.2, although its Figure 2 caption still describes consecutive-frame residuals. Core quantization and commitment-loss mathematics remain equivalent, and most added encoder/decoder equations formalize the existing procedure. Neither version introduces theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: V3 drops progressive curriculum training as a main contribution and centers the paper on video tokenization. The headline reconstruction claim changes from comparable OmniTokenizer fidelity at one-quarter the tokens to superior compressed reconstruction, including comparisons against LARP. Image reconstruction remains a claimed capability, but its headline result disappears from the abstract.

C2.justification: V3 replaces inability to exploit image pretraining with difficulty learning intertwined information as an explanation for non-decoupled performance. It changes the language-model interpretation from stronger Qwen embeddings being preferable to their extra complexity being insufficiently cost-effective, and introduces a generator scaling interpretation. The stated limitation concerning precise semantic understanding and VQA remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 revises the training hyperparameter table, adds tokenizer parameter counts, and specifies GCN word-pair categories. It no longer explicitly identifies the caption-generation model, states that codebook embeddings are frozen, or identifies OmniTokenizer as the proxy encoder/pixel decoder. Most architecture, preprocessing, codebook-size, and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: LARP becomes a central reference throughout the introduction, background, preliminary formulation, and comparisons, repositioning the contribution against holistic query-based video tokenizers. TokenFlow is also added, while curriculum-learning, distillation, and several other references disappear. This substantially changes research positioning rather than merely updating bibliography metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method are rewritten around decoupled video queries. V3 reorganizes the method into spatial and temporal tokenization explanations, removes the dedicated progressive-training subsection, and shortens training discussion in the appendix. SweetTokenizer/CQAE/LLC terminology changes throughout to SweetTok/DQAE/MLC.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figures 1–2, incorporates the module diagram into a comparative pipeline overview, adds LARP reconstruction displays, and restructures generation examples. Main tables gain parameter/type columns and resolution-based shading. Figure 6 redisplays selected existing appendix image reconstructions; appendix Table 8 is replaced and the image-generation figure removed. Other appendix reconstruction and semantic visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 provides more informative evidence through similarly compressed LARP comparisons, explicit model-size/resolution distinctions, and complementary reconstruction metrics (Tables 1–3 and 8). These support a limited quality improvement independently of higher scores. Gains are constrained by reduced implementation disclosure and unresolved reporting inconsistencies, including TiTok's text/table rFID mismatch and conflicting training batch sizes.
